title: Meng Wanzhou and the Two Michaels

text.brief: State security officers detained Michael Kovrig in Beijing on December 10, 2018, nine days after Canada arrested Meng Wanzhou at American request.
text.record: Meng, Huawei's chief financial officer, faced American charges of bank fraud tied to sanctions on Iran. The Party detained Michael Spavor the same week and held both men for 1,019 days ([Sentencing of Canadian Citizen Michael Spavor (U.S. Department of State statement)](https://2021-2025.state.gov/sentencing-of-canadian-citizen-michael-spavor/)). A court sentenced Spavor to eleven years for espionage in August 2021 ([Sentencing of Canadian Citizen Michael Spavor (U.S. Department of State statement)](https://2021-2025.state.gov/sentencing-of-canadian-citizen-michael-spavor/)). Meng reached a deferred prosecution agreement with the Justice Department on September 24, 2021 ([CRS report R47620 on Canada-PRC relations (congress.gov)](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/R/PDF/R47620/R47620.3.pdf); [Radio-Canada International, September 24, 2021: B.C. court drops extradition case after Meng Wanzhou enters deferred prosecution agreement in U.S. (media only)](https://ici.radio-canada.ca/rci/en/news/1826820/b-c-court-drops-extradition-case-after-meng-wanzhou-enters-deferred-prosecution-agreement-in-u-s-)). She flew home, and the two Michaels flew to Canada within hours.
text.reading: The Party could not seize the prosecutor, so it seized two citizens of the ally that made the arrest, which is Stratagem 26. The exchange set a price on every allied citizen on the mainland, and the clock ran on the hostages rather than on the defendant.
text.gapText: Architecture Governance. The United States asked an ally to make an arrest and had no plan to protect the ally's citizens from reprisal.
text.fix: Agree with allies in advance on how to answer hostage-taking, and treat a seized allied citizen as a charge on the whole alliance.
